The threat actor created local administrator accounts on previously compromised third-party organizations for reconnaissance and to remotely access Energy Sector targets
The threat actor used Windows’ Scheduled Tasks and batch scripts to execute scr.exe and collect screenshots of systems across the network
The threat actor used batch scripts dc.bat and dit.bat to enumerate hosts, users, and additional information about the environment
The actor used dirsb.bat to gather folder and file names from hosts on the network as part of reconnaissance operations
The actor used batch scripts labeled pss.bat and psc.bat to run the PsExec tool to execute scr.exe across the network and collect screenshots of systems in a text file
The threat actor collected the Windows SYSTEM registry hive file, which contains host configuration information
The threat actor compressed the ntds.dit file and the SYSTEM registry hive they had collected into archives named SYSTEM.zip and comps.zip
The threat actor downloaded tools from a remote server into the network

The threat actor used password-cracking techniques to obtain plaintext passwords from obtained credential hashes, dropping and executing open-source and free password cracking tools such as Hydra, SecretsDump, CrackMapExec, and Python
